newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen lower on Dow fall but tone positive.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen lower on Dow fall but tone positive.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks could see some weakness on Thursday following the lower overnight close on Wall Street but analysts said the underlying tone of the market was still positive and any downside would be met with buying.
Wall Street might cause an initial fall in Hong Kong stocks but sentiment remained bullish ahead of the five-day handover break, said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities.
The Dow industrials fell 68.08 points to 7,689.98 on fears higher oil prices might fuel a U.S. interest rate rise.
"The Hang Seng should hover round the 15,000 mark later today," Cheung said.
The blue-chip index rose 174.06 points, or 1.17 percent, to 15,065.02 on Wednesday. Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index rose 7.33 points to 15,072.35.
Other analysts saw a weaker performance on Thursday.
"Since U.S. stocks were so volatile yesterday and the (U.S.) long bond yield rose to 6.74 percent, these should affect Hong Kong stocks," said Alex Wong, research analyst at Dharmala Securities.
The index would find support at the 14,900 level, he said.
June index futures will expire later on Thursday, which would probably add volatility to the market, brokers said. -- Alison Leung (852) 2843 6369
